post.title: Through the burn
post.body:
May 24, 2025: the Corral Trail Loop from the Corral trailhead, up as far as the first lookout, where I turned around. Marley came along the whole way.

A little before nine I leaned the bike against a pine and took a picture. Green forest, granite boulders scattered between the trunks, low sun coming through.

Twenty minutes later the trees had changed. Behind me in a selfie the forest is burned: grey snags, black trunks, a pile of cut wood, and snow still on the peaks across the valley.

Around half past nine I reached the first lookout, where the burn opens up. Through the dead trees there's Lake Tahoe, a long stretch of blue water with mountains behind it, a little snow on top. Along the dirt road, logs had been cut and stacked, with fresh stumps everywhere. Marley climbed onto one of them and stood looking out, harness on, very pleased with the view. This was where I turned around.

On the way back, twenty minutes on, there was a granite boulder bigger than anything around it, sitting among the burned trunks. Marley got up on a small rock right at its foot, which is the only way to show how big that boulder is.

Just before eleven we were down at a creek. Clear water over rocks, green grass, a log fence along the bank. Helmet off, Marley sitting next to me, both of us looking at the camera.

And yes, I forgot to turn off the tracker app again, so the recording runs on well past the end of the ride.

episode.title: Marley on the rock
episode.script:
Late May, at the Corral trailhead. Blue sky, low sun, and a mountain bike leaning against a pine.

It's a little before nine in the morning. Christian is riding the Corral Trail Loop, up as far as the first lookout, and that's where he'll turn around. The forest around him is green and quiet, with big granite boulders resting between the trunks, as if somebody had left them there and meant to come back.

***

Twenty minutes later the forest looks different. Christian takes a selfie, helmet on, and behind him the trees are grey and black. Burned. Some are still standing, some are on the ground, and one pile has been cut and stacked. Far off, across the valley, there's still snow on the peaks.

By half past nine he's at the first lookout, a wide spot along a dirt road. Through the dead trees there's Lake Tahoe. A long band of blue, mountains on the far side, a little snow on top. Around him the ground is covered in cut logs and fresh stumps, the work of whoever is clearing the burn.

And there's Marley, Christian's dog, along for the whole ride. Brown and white, in a black harness. Marley climbs onto a stump and stands there with her chest out, looking at the same view. She holds the pose long enough for a photo. Most dogs don't.

This is the turnaround.

***

Twenty minutes later, on the way back, there's a boulder. Not one of the ordinary ones from the morning. This one is the size of a small house, pale granite, sitting on its own among the burned trees. At its foot is a small rock, and on the small rock is Marley. That's the only reason anyone can tell how big the boulder really is.

***

The last stop is just before eleven. A creek, running clear over stones. Green grass on the banks, a fence of peeled logs along the edge. Christian's helmet is off. Marley sits next to him, a little squinty in the sun.

Two selfies, two seconds apart. Then, presumably, back on the bike.

The tracker, as usual, didn't get the message. It kept counting long after the ride was over.
